page: UpCloud 24xCPU-96GB is a general-purpose server configured on the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 x86_64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system allocates 24 physical cores with a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio on a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a 1920 GB local SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core metrics and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 decompression rates placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Multi-core performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is also strong, though uncached large-block read and write bandwidths fall into the average tier. Geekbench and Passmark scores across CPU, memory, and database operations consistently rank in the average tier.

This server is suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, and small-scale LLM inference, where it achieves top-tier text generation and prompt processing speeds for small models. The shared CPU allocation model presents a potential performance tradeoff for sustained, high-intensity compute tasks compared to dedicated resources. However, the high-capacity 1920 GB local SSD and balanced 1:4 CPU-to-RAM ratio offer solid resource density for database operations and multi-threaded applications.
